questions.question: Which option correctly represents Displacement Current?
questions.answer: iD = epsilon0 dPhiE/dt
questions.solution: Displacement Current: Changing electric flux acts like current in Maxwell theory. The correct relation is iD = epsilon0 dPhiE/dt.
questions.commonTrap: Not conduction current through gap.
questions.shortcut: Draw the model first, then apply the formula.
options: iD = epsilon0 dPhiE/dt
integral B dl = mu0(I + iD)
Only the average value is required
It is independent of all variables

questions.question: Which option correctly represents Maxwell-Ampere Law?
questions.answer: integral B dl = mu0(I + iD)
questions.solution: Maxwell-Ampere Law: Magnetic field is produced by conduction plus displacement current. The correct relation is integral B dl = mu0(I + iD).
questions.commonTrap: Ignoring iD breaks capacitor continuity.
questions.shortcut: Draw the model first, then apply the formula.
options: integral B dl = mu0(I + iD)
c = 1/sqrt(mu0 epsilon0)
Only the average value is required
It is independent of all variables

questions.question: Which option correctly represents Speed of EM Waves?
questions.answer: c = 1/sqrt(mu0 epsilon0)
questions.solution: Speed of EM Waves: Vacuum speed follows from field constants. The correct relation is c = 1/sqrt(mu0 epsilon0).
questions.commonTrap: This is speed in vacuum.
questions.shortcut: Draw the model first, then apply the formula.
options: c = 1/sqrt(mu0 epsilon0)
c = f lambda
Only the average value is required
It is independent of all variables

questions.question: Which option correctly represents Wave Relation?
questions.answer: c = f lambda
questions.solution: Wave Relation: Speed equals frequency times wavelength. The correct relation is c = f lambda.
questions.commonTrap: Frequency does not change in refraction, speed/wavelength do.
questions.shortcut: Draw the model first, then apply the formula.
options: c = f lambda
E0/B0 = c
Only the average value is required
It is independent of all variables

questions.question: Which option correctly represents E-B Ratio?
questions.answer: E0/B0 = c
questions.solution: E-B Ratio: Fields in EM wave have fixed amplitude ratio. The correct relation is E0/B0 = c.
questions.commonTrap: Ratio has units of speed.
questions.shortcut: Draw the model first, then apply the formula.
options: E0/B0 = c
uE = 1/2 epsilon0 E^2
Only the average value is required
It is independent of all variables

questions.question: Which option correctly represents Electric Field Energy Density?
questions.answer: uE = 1/2 epsilon0 E^2

questions.question: Which option correctly represents EM Wave Intensity?
